findings.description: The planned E2E test variant (test_v1_e2e_with_real_audio_features) to exercise real audio extraction in the full workflow was not implemented. The existing test_v1_upload_analysis_and_report_flow still monkeypatches extract_features(), so real librosa/essentia integration is not verified in the E2E context.
findings.suggestion: Real audio extraction is tested separately via test_real_audio_feature_extraction_with_librosa(). Add the E2E variant in Phase 2 if needed for deeper integration confidence, or defer as documented in the plan as optional if time was constrained.

findings.description: The CI workflow attempts to install essentia with continue-on-error, which is correct for this complex library. However, there is no post-install assertion or log to document whether essentia was successfully installed for reference.
findings.suggestion: Optional: Add a CI step after essentia install that logs 'essentia installed successfully' or 'essentia install skipped; key detection tests will use unavailable status' so CI logs document the actual state.

findings.description: The feature_extraction_completed log in audio.py includes librosa_available and essentia_available flags but does not log the actual library versions. The _version() function exists and is used in the feature dict, but version strings are not included in the log entry.
findings.suggestion: Optional enhancement: Include version strings in the log entry for future debugging. This is low priority; the availability flags are sufficient for Phase 1.

findings.description: The README mentions establishing a Phase 1 coverage baseline and notes 'to be filled after initial test run' but does not include actual coverage percentages.
findings.suggestion: Run `pytest --cov=backend --cov-report=term-missing` locally after Phase 1 is approved and add the final baseline percentages to README.

findings.description: The video rendering test skips silently in local development when FFmpeg is not installed. This is correct for flexibility but means developers might unknowingly ship without video coverage.
findings.suggestion: Optional: Document in README's Local Setup section that 'FFmpeg is required for video rendering tests; tests will skip silently if unavailable. For full test coverage, install FFmpeg: apt-get install ffmpeg (Linux), brew install ffmpeg (macOS), or download from ffmpeg.org (Windows).'
